dominant_strengths: Striking volumetric red gradient hero feels physical and brand-aligned, giving the dark canvas a memorable, distinctive visceral hook
Floating pill nav with crisp sans-serif, generous tracking, and Apple glyph download CTA reads as confidently mac-native
Restrained palette of black, white, and saturated red enforces strong hierarchy and lets the headline carry the page
dominant_weaknesses: Headline typography is competent but generic; weight, size, and tracking don't match the boldness of the abstract artwork behind it
Two stacked download buttons under the fold compete with the top-right Download CTA, creating redundant action hierarchy
Composition relies almost entirely on the gradient render; layout itself is conventional centered-hero with little structural creativity
fix_priorities: Push headline scale and weight further, or set in a more distinctive display cut to match the visual intensity of the artwork
Resolve dual-CTA conflict: demote the nav download or unify Mac/Windows into a single smart button
Introduce secondary structural elements (product screenshot, command palette mock) so the page sells capability beyond mood
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral dominates via the gradient spectacle, behavioral is solid through clear nav and downloads, reflective is thinner because the page tells little about what Raycast actually does.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—it reads unmistakably as a polished mac-native launcher marketing site, though it leans more on atmosphere than on demonstrating the product.
